entityDescription: Charles University is one of the oldest European universities and it is currently the largest research institution in the Czech Republic. It is divided into 17 economically independent units – faculties. The space research is carried out at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics that is undoubtedly an important research institutions not only in the Czech Republic but also in the European context. It concentrates predominantly on the fundamental basic research in nearly all directions of present Mathematics, Physics and Computer Science but applied research is under way in many areas as well. This research is carried out usually in frame of joint project with different institutions ranging from institutes of the Academy of Sciences to industrial enterprises that are interested in modern materials or techniques (see: http://www.mff.cuni.cz/). A random selection of interesting research directions can be listed as follows: - investigations of surface properties of different materials with motivation to find effective catalysts was awarded by Japanese and American patents on technique of fabrication of low-cost catalysts for fuel cells. - research of the microstructure and properties of advanced materials for structural and functional applications. The main target is the investigation of the relation between microstructure, and mechanical and thermal properties of metals, alloys, intermetallic compounds, metal matrix composites and materials with fine and ultrafine microstructures. A large effort is also devoted to complex investigation of physical aspects of plastic deformation (involving theory, modelling and experiment) and to investigation of phase transformations in metallic materials. - structure and microscopic electronic properties of thin films, magnetic multilayers and intermetallic compounds are investigated by methods using scattering of X-rays, synchrotron radiation and neutron beams. Bulk material properties, especially the magnetic behavior, transport, thermodynamic and cohesive properties, phase transitions and diffusion processes are investigated over a broad range of temperatures, external pressures and magnetic fields. Theoretical studies of quantum coherence in semiconductor alloys excited by femtosecond pulses, mesoscopic theory of wear and physics of granular systems complete our fields of interest. - space research connected with development of measuring devices for satellites or space missions started at the very beginning of space era. The devices participated in more than 15 missions and this trend continues. - study of homogeneous and heterogenous macromolecular systems on sub-molecular, molecular and supra-molecular level. A particular attention is devoted to polymer networks, gels, polyelectrolytes and liquid-crystalline substances; these systems are studied by mechanical and electrical relaxation spectroscopy and by other physical methods. Electron states of polymers, organic and anorganic semiconductors and their photophysical properties (photogeneration of charge, electroluminiscence, photovoltaic voltage, etc.) are investigated by optical methods. - research in the mathematical analysis covers all important directions: theory of functions of real as well as complex variables, theory and applications of partial differential equations, functional analysis and topology, potential theory and some aspects of mathematical physics. - mathematical statistics and probability research cover non-parametric, robust and asymptotic statistics, theory of extremes, stochastic stereology and space statistics, bio-statistics, stochastic modeling in economy and many others. A detailed information can be found in the web pages of the faculty departments.

entityDescription:
Norsk Regnesentral (Norwegian Computing Center, NR) is a non-profit research institute that performs contract research in the following research fields: Statistical modeling, Information technology, Remote sensing an Image analysis.
NR is a private, independent, non-profit research foundation. NR is one of the technical and industrial research institutes in Norway. Research institutes carry out approximately 25% of the research in Norway. NR receives a small basic funding from the government through the Research Council of Norway but depends mainly on funding for all the research projects from the organization that benefits from the research. Typical clients are large companies, smaller private companies, public sector and international organizations. 
NR was established in 1952. Until 1970 an important part of the activity was to perform mathematical computations for other organizations. After 1970 NR has been a methodological research institute. In 1985, NR became an independent institute and moved to its present location in 1988. NR is famous for inventing the first object oriented programming language Simula in the 1960s. NR has worked with data communication since 1963, the Internet since 1973 and multimedia since1994. NR started working with statistics in 1952, remote sensing in 1982, geostatistics and petroleum in 1983, marine resources in 1988 and electricity prices and finance in 1994. 
NR has been a leading research and development institute in Earth Observation since Norway started to focus on satellite remote sensing in the beginning of the 1980's. The institute's main role has since then been to do research and development of methodologies for analysis of digital remote sensing data, in particular methodologies for semi-automatic and automatic classification, parameter retrieval and object recognition.

entityDescription: At Clyde Space we are passionate about space technology, especially when it comes to making that technology smaller, higher performance, more cost effective and with shorter lead-times. Started in 2005, Clyde Space has become a leading supplier of small spacecraft systems and platforms, particularly in the CubeSat market. We typically supply high performance power subsystems, DC-DC Converters, lithium polymer batteries and high efficiency solar panels, and have developed a complete end-to-end nanosatellite mission capability. Clyde Space's first complete satellite, the 3U CubeSat UKube-1, was successfully launched in July 2014. Now working on several further CubeSat missions - including ESA's PICASSO CubeSat - Clyde Space moved to new, larger facilities at the end of 2014 and is now expanding and equipped for high-volume nanosatellite manufacturing. Everything we do at Clyde Space is governed by our values: Excellence, Passionate People, Innovation, Building Trust-based Relationships and Integrity. Our long-term reputation depends on doing the right thing within these core values; even if it adversely affects our business in the short-term.

entityDescription: NTNU Samfunnsforskning AS is a non-profit Research Company owned 100% by Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU). The activity is project based and the majority of the approx. 100 employees are working with social science research. Yearly production is approx. NOK 137 million. CIRiS - Center for Interdisciplinary Research in Space is a department at NTNU Samfunnsforskning AS established in 2007. The department's mandate is to focus on research, development and innovation related to Life Support Systems and sustainable food production for Space and Earth applications. The main activities today are life science research and payload development for the International Space Station (ISS) and Life support systems for long duration human space exploration mission within the ESA program. Research related to the impact manned space exploration and the civil space industry have on our society on Earth is also a priority area within the department.

COWI 

COWI is a leading consulting company that creates value for customers, people and society through our unique 360° approach and with more than 6,500 colleagues working in a broad range of specialist fields. Many projects are carried out in cooperation across the organisation to achieve synergies and access domain knowledge that benefits the projects.

All of our services are defined in COWI’s quality management system, which is based on our long-standing experience in project implementation, and which is certified according to the ISO 9001 standard. This ensures a high level of quality in all processes.

With offices all over the world, we draw on global project experience and competencies when handling projects, irrespective of their size or location in the world. At any given moment, we are involved in more than 17,000 projects.

We have more than 80 years of experience in the consulting business, and together with our customers, we create coherence in tomorrow’s sustainable societies.

GIS & IT

We add maximum business value for our customers by supplying unique solutions in close collaboration with other COWI business units and partners. 

We handle development and consultancy projects for customers in both the private and the public sector, both at home and abroad.

Our services include: 
- Handling of geospatial data, satellite data and GIS products
- IT management consultancy
- Development of business critical GIS and IT solutions.
- Support and operations.

entityDescription:
Leonardo is a global player in the high-tech sectors and a major operator worldwide in the Aerospace, Defence and Security sectors. Leonardo is based in Italy, has about 45.600 employees, of whom about 37% abroad.

Based on the dual application of technologies, Leonardo designs and produces systems, services and integrated solutions both for the defence sector and for public and private customers of the civil sector, both in Italy and abroad. The wide range of defence and security solutions that Leonardo offers Governments, private citizens and Institutions includes every possible intervention scenario: airborne and terrestrial, naval and maritime, space and cyberspace. 
Leonardo operates in about 20 countries with offices and industrial plants in all of the five continents and can rely on a very large network of subsidiaries, joint ventures and international partnerships, with significant industrial presence in three main markets, United Kingdom, Poland and United States and structured partnerships in the most important high potential markets in the world.

Space Activities are carried out through the Optronics and Space Equipment Line of Business of Electronics ITA Business Unit.

Space business in Italy takes place in Campi Bisenzio, Nerviano and Pomezia, where all design development, manufacturing and testing activities are carried out on an area totalling 18.000 m2 a large amount of which hosts clean rooms and laboratories equipped with appropriate space simulators and test facilities to support the production areas. 
The Space Equipment Business Area of Optronics and Space Line of Business has in charge the design, development, test and marketing of the whole lifecycle for space products (manufacturing, PA and procurement are centralized within the Division). For its products/processes/services Leonardo operates a quality system certified in conformity with ISO 9001-2008 and EN 9100-2009.

entityDescription:
Crisa, an Airbus Defence and Space company, has a strong reputation as high technology firm in Space (avionics for satellites, launchers and space vehicles) and Ground Segment both in civil and Defence applications. 

The company's activities cover a wide product range like: 
- System engineering
- Launcher electronics
- Launcher avionics integration
- Driving electronics
- Electric propulsion electronics
- Proximity and video electronics
- Instrument Controllers
- Digital Signal Processors
- Security Units
- On board computers
- Remote terminal units
- Thermal Control Unit
- Control momentum Gyro electronics
- Pyrotechnic Control & Fuse Box
- Harness
- Fiber Optic Sensing
- Power distribution units
- Power control units
- Power Subsystems
- DC/DC converters
- Cooler electronics
- Microelectronics
- Payload Data Handling
- P/L Mechanism Control electronics
- Active Antenna control electronics
- Flight software

Crisa has contributed to most of the European Space Agency (ESA) programs with more than 35 years experience and 1200 electronic units flown into 467 space missions. 
At the moment, the company is working on key programs like Ariane 6 and Vega-C launchers and Eurostar Neo platform. Also in well-known missions like MSR ERO, PILOT, Copernicus, Smile or Orion among others.

Crisa has expanded its engineering and project management skills in other ground segment projects. Some of these projects include network architecture design for secure communications; control center implementation, operation and maintenance; archiving and cataloguing systems; remote operation. Crisa is able to provide reliable electronics designed and manufactures for harsh environment like space or under no-maintenance conditions. The company has also a strong knowledge of system engineering and project management. 

Crisa in Tres Cantos employs about 500 qualified employees.

entityDescription: At Omnisys we strive to engineer the most technically advanced, affordable and user-oriented technology solutions possible. Most of our products and services are developed in close collaboration with leading institutes in the field of space and satellite research. We specialize in development and production of high performance electronics hardware for the space industry, yet our technology and test labs can also be used for other scientific, security and med-tech applications. Major clients and partners are the European Space Agency, the Swedish National Space Board, Chalmers University of Technology, OHB Sweden and the European Southern Observatory. We have delivered space flight hardware for a number of Swedish and European satellite projects such as ODIN, SMART-1, PRISMA, SWI at JUICE, Metop SG and the payload AWS radiometer instrument.

entityName: ONERA. Office National d'Etudes et Recherches Aérospatiales
entityDescription: Onera, First Aerospace Research Player in France Onera (Office National d'Etudes et Recherches Aérospatiales) is the French national aerospace research center. It is a public research establishment, with eight major facilities in France and about 2,000 employees, including 1,500 scientists, engineers and technicians. It has moved its headquarters from Châtillon to Palaiseau in 2014. Onera was originally created by the French government in 1946, and assigned six key missions: Direct and conduct aeronautical research Support the commercialization of this research by national and European industry Construct and operate the associated experimental facilities Supply industry with high-level technical analyses and other services. Perform technical analyses for the government Train researchers and engineers Application-Oriented Research All of this research is keyed to applications. Whether the research has short, medium or long-term goals, it is designed to support the competitiveness and creativity of the aerospace and defense industries. The research carried out at Onera results in computation codes, methods, tools, technologies, materials and other products and services which are used to design and manufacture everything to do with aerospace: Civil aircraft Military aircraft Helicopters and tiltrotors Propulsion systems Orbital systems Space transport Missile systems Defense systems Networked systems and security systems 60% of Funding from Contracts Onera's funding comes from two sources: 60%: contract research for industry and agencies 40%: annual subsidy from the French government The subsidy primarily finances long-term research, which lays the groundwork for future developments. Research contracts finance medium and short-term work, closer to the application. The strategic challenge for Onera is to organize this broad knowledge stream, ranging from the acquisition of knowledge to transferring it to industry.

entityDescription: Critical Software supports mission critical information systems across diverse markets including aerospace and defence. A high-growth company founded in Portugal in 1998, it does well over half its business internationally. Critical Software opened a US Office in 2000 and a UK subsidiary, Critical Software Technologies Ltd, in 2004. The company has a solid record of achievement for government and blue-chip clients. It has successfully released products worldwide in both niche and mass markets. Critical Software has developed strong expertise in a number of key fields including:- * Development of High Integrity Software for Aerospace (e.g. Avionics) * Independent Verification and Validation of Critical Software * Software for the Ground Segment of Satellite Systems * Networking and High Performance Computing * Enterprise Applications Integration In the UK, the company will focus initially on development of dependable software and Independent Software Verification and Validation (ISVV). Critical Software has specialist skills and products for ISVV and also Reliability, Availability, Maintainability & Safety (RAMS); Fault Detection, Isolation & Recovery (FDIR) and Product Assurance. Critical Software Technologies operates a quality system accredited to ISO 9001:2000 with TickIT. The company maintains strong R & D relationships with leading research and educational institutions.
